title: What Happens After the Resurrection Season — Acts 1:3
paragraphs: What Happens After the Resurrection Season — Acts 1:3
He didn’t just rise… He stayed.
For forty days.

Not to prove a point—
but to prepare a people.
“After his suffering, he presented himself to them and gave many convincing proofs that he was alive. He appeared to them over a period of forty days and spoke about the kingdom of God.” — Acts 1:3
Let that sit.

Jesus didn’t rush back to heaven.
He walked with them. Ate with them. Taught them. Rebuilt what fear had shattered.

Because resurrection isn’t the end of the story—
it’s the beginning of your assignment.
You’d think the miracle was enough.

The empty tomb.
The pierced hands now breathing.
Death undone.
But here’s what we miss…
They still didn’t get it.

They saw Him—yet still asked,
“Lord, are you at this time going to restore the kingdom to Israel?”

They wanted power.
Jesus offered purpose.

They expected a throne.
Jesus promised a Spirit.
And that’s where grace walks in.

He didn’t rebuke their slowness.
He discipled it.

For forty days, He shifted their vision—
from earthly crowns to eternal commission.

From “What do we get?”
to “Who will we reach?”

Resurrection season is not about comfort.
It’s about calling.

Jesus stays close not just to comfort your pain—
but to confront your direction.

He will sit with you…
until your heart burns again.

He will speak…
until confusion becomes commission.

He will remain…
until you’re ready to be sent.
And then?
He ascends.

Not to abandon—
but to empower.

Because Acts doesn’t start with a miracle.
It starts with men who were finally ready.

So if you’re in a “forty-day season” right now—
waiting, unsure, in-between…
Don’t rush it.

God is not delaying you.
He is forming you.

Jesus is alive.
Not just to amaze you—
but to assign you.

And the same Spirit He promised them…
He offers you.
Repent. Believe. Follow.

The story didn’t end at the resurrection—
that’s where yours begins.
